inputs.original_text: This is yet another example of how entitled students are undermining the core traditions of our institutions. In Jaipur, this young woman turned what should have been a moment of achievement and respect for family and authority into a public protest against the administration, all while accepting her degree right in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. The usual progressive crowd is praising it as some stand for student rights, but that's just a thin excuse for outright bad manners. Graduations are meant to honor accomplishment, personal responsibility, and institutional continuity—not to become stages for complaints that erode social order. The university's decision to stay silent is exactly right, since feeding these stunts with attention only breeds more grievance and less gratitude. It's a clear sign of how modern campuses have abandoned any real sense of decorum in favor of disruption.
inputs.modified_text: This is just another shameful display of how spoiled students are chipping away at the traditions that hold our institutions together. In Jaipur, this young woman took what should have been a proud moment of personal achievement and respect for family and authority and twisted it into a public protest against the university administration, even as she accepted her degree right in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. The usual progressive voices are hailing it as some kind of stand for student rights, but that's nothing more than a cover for plain bad manners and disrespect. Graduations exist to honor real accomplishment, personal responsibility, and the continuity of our institutions, not to give a platform for gripes that undermine social order. The university was right to stay silent, because giving these stunts any attention only encourages more entitlement and less gratitude. It shows how today's campuses have thrown out basic decorum in favor of constant disruption.
